headline: Approved a pilot camera program on school buses, a $3,725 budget modification, and grant and donation acceptances.
summary: Project LEARN gave the first Spotlight on Excellence presentation. Members approved a pilot camera program on school buses, a $3,725 budget modification, and donations from the Greater Lowell Community Foundation. They also approved four travel requests and the disposal of surplus equipment.

Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
LOWELL SCHOOL COMMITTEE 
REGULAR MEETING MINUTES 
, 2025 
 
 
 
 
Date: October 21, 2026 
Time: 6:30PM 
Location: City Council Chamber, 375 Merrimack Street, 2nd Floor, Lowell, MA 01852 
____________________________________________________________________________________ 
Members of the public can view the meeting via LTC.  Those wishing to speak about a specific agenda 
item must register in advance by emailing the Superintendent.  Please include the agenda item, as well 
as your phone number and email address so we can provide a Zoom link for access. The email address is 
skeo@lowell.k12.ma.us. If you do not have access to email, you may contact us at 978-674-4324. All 
requests must be submitted by 2:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. 
 
1. SALUTE TO FLAG 
 
2. ROLL CALL 
 
On a roll call at 6:30 p.m., members present were, namely: Ms. Martin, Ms. McFadden, Mr. Bahou, 
Mr. Conway, Mayor Gitschier and Mr. Lay. Ms. Delrossi arrived at 6:44 p.m. 
 
3. SPECIAL ORDER OF BUSINESS 
 
3.1. Spotlight on Excellence: Project LEARN 
 
The first Spotlight on Excellence featured Project LEARN. Ms. Rivera-Quintal, Interim Executive Director, 
informed the Committee that Project LEARN is a nonprofit organization dedicated to envisioning a 
future in which every person in Lowell has access to education, develops the skills and social capital 
needed to succeed, and can achieve their full potential. She then highlighted several programs that 
Project LEARN and Lowell Public Schools are currently working together on. 
 
4. MINUTES 
 
4.1. The Approval of the Minutes of the Regularly Scheduled Lowell School Committee Meeting of 
October 7, 2026 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to accept and place on file the minutes of the Regularly Scheduled School 
Committee meeting that was held on October 7, 2026; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The 
motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
5. PERMISSION TO ENTER 
 
5.1. Permission to Enter – October 21, 2026 
 
Mr. Lay moved to approve the Permission to Enter; the motion was seconded by Ms. McFadden. The 
motion passed with 7 yeas.
(Page 2 of 5) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
 
6. MEMORIALS 
 
6.1. Amy L. Cloutier, Paraprofessional at the McAuliffe Elementary School 
 
7. MOTIONS 
 
7.1. [By Mayor Gitschier]: Request the Superintendent have the finance department outline when the 
last paycheck of SY26-2027 will be furnished and when the first paycheck of SY27-28 will be furnished. 
What is the number of days in between pay periods. 
 
Mayor Gitschier moved to approve; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed 
with 7 yeas. 
 
7.2. [By Mayor Gitschier]: Req. Superintendent provide a path forward to implement a pilot camera 
program on a selection of school buses assigned to transporting Lowell students. 
 
Mr. Bahou requested that the Committee be provided with information regarding the cost of a ticket for 
a violation, whether a warning would be issued for a first offense, how the revenue from ticket fines 
would be distributed among the School Department, the company, and other parties, and whether the 
violation would be attached to the driver's license. 
 
Mayor Gitschier moved to approve; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed 
with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Delrossi). 
 
7.3. [By Fred Bahou]: Request Superintendent to have proper department explore the possibility of 
moving LPS 4th and 5th floor administrative offices from current location on Merrimack Street to 
another location in the city to alleviate the cost of leasing the current space. 
 
Mr. Lay also suggested including the FRC on the first floor. 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to approve; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 
absent (Ms. Delrossi). 
 
8. SUBCOMMITTEES 
 
8.1. The Approval of the Minutes of the Joint Finance & Curriculum and Instruction Subcommittee 
Meeting of October 7, 2026. 
 
Chairperson Bahou, Chair of the Finance Subcommittee, informed the Committee that current staff 
devices are nearing the end of their recommended operational lifespan, resulting in potential security 
vulnerabilities, software and operating system incompatibilities, and decreased performance. He noted 
that the current curriculum relies heavily on digital resources and web-based multimedia tools. The 
proposed replacement devices for teachers would be MacBook Neos, at an estimated cost of $800 per 
device. He explained that teachers have been using their current district-issued devices for nearly seven 
years and that Apple discontinues software updates after seven years, increasing the risk of security
(Page 3 of 5)

issues. The Subcommittee recommended postponing action until additional information could be 
obtained regarding the possibility of securing a lower interest rate on the lease. 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to accept the report as a report of progress; the motion was seconded by Ms. 
McFadden. The motion passed with 5 yeas, 2 absent (Mr. Conway, Ms. Delrossi). 
 
9. REPORTS OF THE SUPERINTENDENT 
 
9.1. Home Education 
 
Superintendent Skinner recommended that the following parents/guardians be allowed to home 
educate their child:  
Djose Zamor 
Brandi Woolf 
 
Mr. Lay moved to approve Home Education; the motion was seconded by Mr. Bahou. The motion 
passed with 7 yeas. 
 
10. NEW BUSINESS 
 
10.1. Approval to Accept and Expend Allocated FY27 Award 
 
These grant funds have been secured by the Lowell Public Schools through the Massachusetts 
Department of Elementary and Secondary Education. 
 
Ms. Martin moved to approve, accept and expend the allocated FY27 awards; the motion was 
seconded by Ms. Delrossi. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
10.2. Budget Modification Request 
 
Mr. Lay moved to approve the budget modification in the amount of $3,725; the motion was 
seconded by Ms. McFadden. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
10.3. Letter of Approval for Accepting Donation from Greater Lowell Community Foundation (GLCF) 
 
The Lowell Public Schools received a donation from the GLCF for the following:  
 
➢ $1,000 to sponsor the 2027 Regional Knowledge Bowl 
➢ $12,500 through the Newell Flather Legacy Fund, from the Theodore Edson Parker Foundation, 
to support Vital Skills: Youth Safety Training & Career Readiness programming at the Butler 
Middle School 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept and approve the donation from the Greater Lowell Community 
Foundation (GLCF); the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 7 yeas.
(Page 4 of 5) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
 
10.4. Request for Approval to Recycle or Dispose of Surplus and Unserviceable Equipment 
Approval is requested to recycle and dispose of surplus school equipment and technology items 
currently stored within Lowell Public Schools. A comprehensive assessment of the items was conducted 
on September 28, 2026, and the items were determined to be either beyond economical repair, 
unserviceable, or obsolete. Based on the MIS Department’s assessment and best knowledge, none of 
the individual items listed have a current market value exceeding $5,000. 
Mr. Bahou moved to approve the recycling or disposing of surplus and unserviceable equipment; the 
motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
11. CONVENTION/CONFERENCE REQUESTS 
 
11.1. Out of State Overnight Travel - AFJROTC Drill Team Daytona Beach, FL 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to bundle & approve the convention/conference requests; the motion was 
seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
11.2. Overnight Out of State - Winterguard International Competition Tom River, NJ 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to bundle & approve the convention/conference requests; the motion was 
seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
11.3. Out of State Overnight Travel - WGI Competition Dayton, Ohio 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to bundle & approve the convention/conference requests; the motion was 
seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
11.4. Overnight Request - MASBO Conference Falmouth, MA 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to bundle & approve the convention/conference requests; the motion was 
seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
12. PROFESSIONAL PERSONNEL 
 
12.1. The Members of the United Teachers of Lowell Hereby Donate twelve [12] sick leave days to 
Chelsea Morel, Sullivan School Teacher and [14] fourteen sick leave days to Corey Silva, Greenhalge 
School Paraprofessional. 
 
Mr. Lay moved to approve the professional personnel; the motion was seconded by Ms. Martin. The 
motion passed with 7 yeas.
(Page 5 of 5) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
13. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
 
13.1. An Executive Session may be called to discuss collective bargaining, strategies and/or possible litigation 
under Open Meeting Law, Chapter 30A, Section 21 (A) (B), 2, 3 of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts 
General Laws. Open meeting discussion may have a detrimental effect on the bargaining or litigating position 
of the public body. Item: 
1. Negotiations with Unions and discussion of potential courses of action related to Facilities’ 
leases and uses, in consideration of benefits of proposed legal notices, actions, and studies.  
Mr. Conway moved to recess at 7:05 p.m. and to enter into Executive Session for the purpose of 
discussing collective bargaining, strategies and/or possible litigation under open meeting law, Chapter 
30A, Section 21 (A) (B), 2, 3 of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts General Laws for negotiations 
with unions and discussion of potential courses of action related to facilities’ leases and uses, in 
consideration of benefits of proposed legal notices, actions, and studies, of which open meeting 
discussion may have a detrimental effect on the bargaining or litigating position of the public body, 
and to adjourn from Executive Session; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with   
7 yeas. 
4. ADJOURNMENT 
 
Ms. Fadden moved to adjourn from Executive Session at 8:26 p.m.; the motion was seconded by Mr. 
Bahou. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Delrossi). 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Liam Skinner, Superintendent and 
Secretary to the Lowell School Committee
